subject: Geofence hosting & private connectivity — confirmation and evidence
messages:
From: Grace Li <grace.li@zephyrcorp.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: security@zephyrcorp.com
Date: Sun, 7 Sep 2025 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Geofence hosting & private connectivity — initial questions

Hi Aditya,

Thanks for the demo last week. Before we progress to procurement, our security team needs a short set of confirmations around data residency and private connectivity for Redwood Private. Specific asks:

- Can you confirm whether customer workloads can be constrained to EU-only physical hosts and that logs/analytics can be stored in-region?
- Do you support private connectivity (PrivateLink / VPC peering) into our VPC, and is traffic egress from your control plane to be restricted to our region?
- KMS routing: can we supply our own KMS (bring-your-own-key) and ensure keys remain in our HSM region?
- Any short-form evidence (network diagram, KMS routing summary, SOC 2 attestation link) we can hand to procurement?

We have a tight timeline — if you can get back with confirmation + attachments by EOD Tuesday (9/9) that would help.

Best,
Grace
Grace Li
Security Engineer | Zephyr Corp

--

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 8 Sep 2025 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Geofence hosting & private connectivity — initial questions

Hi Grace —

Thanks for the clear list. Looping in Evelyn (solutions) and Karthik (security) to provide the technical confirmations and the evidence files. Short answers up front:

- Yes — Redwood Private can be deployed in an EU-only region and configured so customer workloads, KV caches, and logs are stored in-region.
- Yes — we support private connectivity (VPC peering or PrivateLink-style endpoints) with customer-managed routing; we can restrict egress to customer-specified subnets/regions.
- Yes — BYOK supported; KMS policy routing keeps keys in the customer's HSM/KMS region; Redwood uses envelope encryption and does not persist plaintext outside the chosen region.

We will attach a network diagram, a one-page KMS routing summary, and a link to our SOC 2 attestation. Evelyn will add a couple of implementation notes for your infra team.

Would you like a brief technical call tomorrow morning to walk the diagram?

Cheers,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

--
Attachments: none
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>
To: Grace Li <grace.li@zephyrcorp.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Sep 2025 10:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Geofence hosting & private connectivity — initial questions

Grace —

Attaching the network diagram and a short KMS routing summary as requested. Key implementation notes below (high level):

- Deployment isolation: For Redwood Private we provision control-plane components in a management VPC (customer-owned or Redwood-hosted per contract). Model-serving nodes (inference runtime) are created only in the customer-specified region (EU) and tagged to prevent cross-region scheduling.

- Data/evidence: Application logs, usage metrics, and KV caches are written to region-scoped storage (S3-equivalent) and retention policies are configurable per tenant. Audit logs for control-plane actions are available with region-scoped retention.

- Private connectivity: We support two patterns: (1) customer VPC peering with static route tables (recommended for highest throughput) and (2) PrivateLink-style endpoints for control-plane APIs. All ingress/outgress for inference traffic is configurable to remain within the region; we provide example route tables in the diagram.

- KMS / BYOK: We support customer-managed KMS keys. The runtime performs envelope encryption; the DEK never leaves the node without encryption by the customer KMS. We provide a KMS routing policy that binds keys to an IAM role scoped to the EU region.

- Fallback modes: If a region's capacity is constrained, we can configure strict region-only policies (fail requests) or soft-fallback (route to a designated fallback region) — you can pick the behavior in the deployment policy.

Attachments included: redwood_vpc_network_diagram.pdf (diagram + example route tables), kms-routing-summary.txt (one-page), soc2-attestation-link.txt (short URL to our auditor attestation).

If useful, I can host a 30-minute walkthrough for your infra/security leads at 11:00 CET tomorrow.

Thanks,
Evelyn Hart
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

--

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Grace Li <grace.li@zephyrcorp.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Sep 2025 15:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Geofence hosting & private connectivity — initial questions

Grace — quick note from security: we have validated the statements Evelyn made against our operational controls. A few explicit confirmations you can provide to procurement/security: 

1) Region-bound storage and compute: all customer data at rest for Redwood Private can be restricted to EU regions; we do not replicate customer tenant data outside the configured geo by default.

2) Key material: BYOK is enforceable via deployment policy. Customer-supplied keys remain in the customer KMS/HSM; Redwood only receives wrapped keys and performs envelope operations.

3) Network segregation: VPC peering and PrivateLink both support enforcing egress path constraints. We can provide a signed diagram and a short attestation letter (PDF) for procurement if needed.

For evidence, use the SOC 2 attestation (link in Evelyn's attachment) and we can provide an internal attestation letter signed by our Head of Security. Let me know if Zephyr needs the attestation to include any custom language re: region-only guarantees.

-Karthik
Head of Security (Acting) | Redwood Inference
